Positivity of Sigma gives the quadratic lower bound lambda*norm(x)^2, from which bounded invertibility must be established; ContinuousLinearMap.inverse returns zero when no continuous equivalence exists and cannot substitute for that proof. variant_reviews.comparison: Both quantities use A=Sigma_lambda^(-1/2)*Sigma*Sigma_lambda^(-1/2). Positivity, spectrum bounded away from zero for Sigma_lambda and the operator-algebra instances are needed before applying the negative half-power; the source is not asking for an unbounded inverse of Sigma itself. Under the trace-class spectral setting, N1 is sum_i tau_i/(tau_i+lambda), while N2 is sqrt(sum_i(tau_i/(tau_i+lambda))^2), not the latter sum without its square root. The nullspace contribution of A is zero. Matrix.trace applies only after a justified finite-dimensional restriction and is not an implementation of the paper's general trace; the continuous-operator norm is also not the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Preserve N1 and N2's separate oracle/power roles and establish summability rather than erasing infinite values through a totalized finite trace.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use ordered distinct pairs i!=j within X and within Y, dividing by N*(N-1) and M*(M-1), and subtract 2/(N*M) times every X-Y cross pair.
